To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the water deficit reduced the starch content in the shoot, but increased the sucrose content in shoot and root of drought tolerant seedlings, which is indicative of its protective role during stress condition.
water deficit induced changes in the activities of carbohydrate metabolising enzymes and carbohydrate content in the seedlings are different in drought-sensitive and drought-tolerat cultivars.
the water deficit increased sucrose content with higher sucrose phosphate synthetase (SPS), lower sucrose synthase (SU) activities, and high invertase activity in shoots of tolerant cultivar (C 306).
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effect of water deficit (stress conditions) on the carbohydrate status and enzymes involved in carbohydrate metabolism (alpha- and beta- amylases, SPS, SS, acid and alkalines invertases) in the seedlings (shoot and root) of wheat cultivars, which differ in drought tolerance.
the effect of water deficit stress on the carbohydrates status and enzymes of the carbohydrate metabolism in wheat cultivars.
the effects of drought stress on the carbohydrate status and enzyme activities of carbohydrate metabolism in wheat seedlings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the higher sucrose content in tolerant cultivar with higher SPS and low SS activities in shoots, higher acid invertase activity and lower beta-amylase activity could be responsible for its drought tolerance.
the higher sucrose content in tolerant cultivar is due to the higher SPS and lower acid invertase and sucrose synthase activities.
water deficit induced higher sucrose content in shoots and roots of C 306, but reduced starch content in shoots.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the drought tolerant cultivar, C 306, was able to maintain higher levels of sucrose in the roots and shoots, and higher SPS activity, which is a key regulatory enzyme in sucrose metabolism, in the shoots, under water deficit conditions.

the water deficit stress induced changes in the activities of enzymes involved in carbohydrate metabolism in wheat seedlings and the tolerant cultivar C 306 showed a better response than sensitive one PBW 343.
the water deficit induced changes in the carbohydrate status and enzyme activities of carbohydrate metabolism in the seedlings were cultivar-specific.
The main takeaway from our work is that

drought-tolerant cultivars can maintain their carbohydrate status by increasing sucrose content with higher sucrose phosphate synthetase activity and lower acid invertase and sucrose synthase activities under water deficit conditions.
drought-tolerant cultivar (C 306), in comparison to sensitive one (PBW 543), showed higher carbohydrate status and higher SPS and acid invertase activity, which are responsible for stress tolerance.
the drought-tolerant wheat cultivar C 306 has a unique characteristic of high acid invertase activity which could be responsible for its drought tolerance.
